notes:
**Mockup comments: thread open in a column** (CHR-1260 / CHR-1261, direction B1). The canvas comment model, applied unchanged to the mockup column view.

**Layout:** the Elements panel is dropped while comments are shown (as in `comments-panel`, decision chr1258). Each variant is a column: a `mockup-column-header` (`variant-badge` letter, title, description, count chips) above the frame. Chips per column: `comment-count-chip` open / `detached` / `resolved` (the last only while Show resolved is on). The Context panel's `comments-count-row` counts the whole mockup.

**Pins:** `comment-pin` centred on the anchored element's top-right corner, inside its variant's frame. Detached pins sit at the frame's top-left. **Thread numbers run across the whole mockup** (#1–#5), not per variant, so "#3" is unique in a discussion. The anchor is `mockup:<mockup>#<variant>.<node-id>` (format owned by the architect).

**Popover:** the same `comment-popover` as on a screen (reply composer, Resolve, ⋯, close). The title carries the `variant-badge` after the number ("#1 A"), so the variant reads without looking at the column. It opens to the right of the pin and may overlap the neighbouring column. It flips left at the stage edge (see `mockup-comments-resolved`) and below when that would cover another pin (see `mockup-comments-detached`).

**Behaviour:** a click on a pin opens its thread. One popover at a time. Esc, close or a click outside closes it. The floating `comment-toolbar` (Select, Comment, Show resolved, Hide pins) is the same as on a screen. The chat icon in the top bar or `C` enters comment mode (→ `mockup-comments-mode`).

**Implementation and a11y:** the same as the canvas. Pins are buttons in DOM order column by column (A → B → C), with aria-label "Comment N on <variant letter>, <node>, <status>" and `aria-expanded`. The popover is `popover="auto"` + `role="dialog"`; focus goes to the composer on open and returns to the pin on close. Anchor positioning uses `position-area: inline-end span-block-end` + `position-try-fallbacks: flip-inline, flip-block`, gated in `@supports (position-area: block-end)`, with a JS getBoundingClientRect fallback.

The frames' inner HTML stands in for the mockup's own raw HTML (outside the ref model). Its literal values are intentional, so the drift warnings on `*-item-*`, `*-total-row` and `*-btn-checkout` are expected.
